title: Compositional and systematic generalization
bottleneck: Models memorize vast patterns yet fail to recombine known concepts into novel structures — the hallmark of human systematicity. Small variations in problem phrasing cause large accuracy drops: OpenAI's o1-preview lost about 30% accuracy on modified Putnam-style problems, with similar drops for GPT-4 and Claude 3.5, revealing shared reliance on memorized templates rather than genuine reasoning. No training method has closed this gap.
why_it_blocks: Real-world deployment is an endless stream of novel situations. If models only work on near-copies of training data, they cannot be trusted in law, finance, or science, where every case differs.
current_state: Benchmarks like PutnamBench and the UnsolvedMath dataset measure true generalization with contamination-free variants. Standard benchmark scores keep climbing while variation-robustness barely moves.
